key_insight: PSyGenTAB generates synthetic clinical tabular data by explicitly optimizing the privacy-utility trade-off, rather than treating privacy as an afterthought.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals and research teams share or model patient data more safely while preserving clinically important patterns needed for AI development.
method: Formulates synthetic data generation as a constrained optimization problem.
Uses the Augmented Lagrangian Method to enforce configurable privacy thresholds during training.
Tests utility with Train-on-Synthetic/Test-on-Real and privacy with record-reproduction and membership-inference audits.
evidence_signal: Across multiple clinically motivated benchmarks, synthetic-data-trained models performed comparably to real-data-trained models, while privacy audits showed less exact record reproduction and stronger resistance to membership inference attacks.
watch_item: The framework still depends on how privacy thresholds are configured in practice, so miscalibration could weaken either utility or protection.
paper_title: PSyGenTAB: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Synthetic Clinical Tabular Data Generation via Constrained Optimization
